turn: Heading anchors in links are now rewritten to GitHub-style slugs. The new `github_anchor` function in `src/links/anchors/slug.py` trims and lowercases the heading, removes characters other than word characters, hyphens and spaces, and then turns spaces into hyphens. I checked it by running it on a handful of sample headings, including ones with punctuation, mixed case and repeated spaces, and the slugs matched what GitHub generates for them. I haven't tested duplicate headings, which GitHub disambiguates with a numeric suffix, and the function doesn't handle them yet. In the same commit I made one small unrelated fix. I noticed that the `re` import in the slug module was being pulled in alongside an unused import, so I removed the unused one to keep the module clean. Next I'll start on "Copy attachments next to each page".

sidefix.title: Remove unused import in slug module
sidefix.what: Removed a leftover unused import next to the `re` import in the slug module so the file stays lint-clean.
